items.claim: Sourcing before compinit errors at every shell start; FAQ gives no ordering caveat
items.consequence: A user who follows the new FAQ paragraph and places `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` in `.zshrc` above `compinit` (or above the oh-my-zsh / zinit / antidote line that runs it) gets `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments` on every new shell and never gets rg completion, because the tail treats "compdef is undefined" as "I am the ci/test-complete harness" and runs `_rg "$@"` at top level. The FAQ text added by this change invites the `source` line without stating the ordering constraint. Verified on zsh 5.8.1: sourcing before compinit exits 1 with that error and `_comps[rg]` stays unset afterwards; sourcing after compinit registers `_rg` correctly. The same heuristic also fails in the mirror direction: a developer whose ~/.zshenv runs compinit makes ci/test-complete take the `compdef` branch, collect zero specs, and fail with 'Failed to get comp_args'.
items.proposed_fix: Two parts. (1) FAQ.md:132-135: say the line must come after `compinit` (or after the framework line that runs it), e.g. "you can add the following to your `$HOME/.zshrc` file, after the line that runs `compinit`:". (2) Optionally stop using `compdef` absence as the harness discriminator in rg.zsh:441, keying the harness branch on the variable ci/test-complete actually sets and making the no-compinit case a no-op or a clear hint: `if [[ $funcstack[1] == _rg ]] || [[ ${_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS-} == (1|t*|y*) ]]; then _rg "$@"; elif (( ${+functions[compdef]} )); then compdef _rg rg; else print -ru2 -- 'rg: zsh completion must be sourced after compinit'; fi`. Verify with ci/test-complete and a `zsh -f` session that sources before and after compinit.

crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh:442 --   _rg "$@"

The pre-change tail `_rg "$@"` produced the same error when sourced before compinit, but the base FAQ never told users to `source` the file from .zshrc; this diff adds that instruction while keeping the error path reachable.

items.claim: Shell prompt `$ ` left inside a code block meant for .zshrc
items.consequence: The paragraph tells the reader to add the block to `$HOME/.zshrc`, but the block carries an interactive `$ ` prompt. Pasted literally, zsh reports `command not found: $` at every shell start and the completion is never loaded. The `fpath=(...)` block added in the same change correctly omits the prompt, so the two blocks are inconsistent.
items.proposed_fix: Replace the block content with `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` (drop the leading `$ `), matching the adjacent `fpath=(...)` block.

items.claim: Name-based `funcstack[1] == _rg` test misclassifies relative source and non-`_rg` installs
items.consequence: The guard decides "am I the autoloaded completion function" by comparing `$funcstack[1]` to the literal `_rg`, but zsh puts the filename as given into funcstack for a sourced file, and the autoloaded function takes whatever name the file has on fpath. Two concrete consequences, both verified on zsh 5.8.1: a user who saved the script as `_rg` per the FAQ and runs `source _rg` from inside that directory gets `_arguments:comparguments:325: can only be called from completion function`, the exact issue #2956 error (while `source ./_rg`, an absolute path, `source <(...)` and `eval` all work); and a file installed on fpath under another name such as `_ripgrep` (legitimate, since compinit binds on the `#compdef rg` header) now takes the `compdef _rg rg` branch on the first TAB and completes nothing until the second TAB, where the pre-change unconditional `_rg "$@"` completed on the first TAB. The evaluation context distinguishes the cases directly and the alternative guard passed the autoload (zsh- and ksh-style), process-substitution, relative-source, and ci/test-complete emulation scenarios in scratch runs.
items.proposed_fix: Discriminate on the evaluation context instead of the frame name: `if [[ ${zsh_eval_context[-1]} != file ]] || (( ! ${+functions[compdef]} )); then` (or, combined with finding #1's harness keying, `[[ ${zsh_eval_context[-1]} == (load|eval)autofunc ]] || [[ ${_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS-} == (1|t*|y*) ]]`). `zsh_eval_context[-1]` is `loadautofunc` for zsh-style autoload, `evalautofunc` for KSH_AUTOLOAD, `file` for any sourced file, and `eval` for eval. Assumption: zsh_eval_context exists on every zsh the script targets (it predates the 5.4 features the script already works around); verify on the oldest supported zsh and re-run ci/test-complete. Bracing the expansions also keeps the test well-formed under KSH_ARRAYS.

evidence: crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh:441 -- if [[ $funcstack[1] == _rg ]] || (( ! $+functions[compdef] )); then
crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh:442 --   _rg "$@"
crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh:1 -- #compdef rg  (compinit binds whichever filename carries this header to `rg`, so the outer autoloaded function need not be named `_rg`)
Scratch run (zsh -f, after compinit): `cd dir; source _rg` -> `_arguments:comparguments:325: can only be called from completion function`, rc=1; `source ./_rg` -> rc=0 and registered.

Adversarial scratch run (only `_ripgrep` on fpath, real compinit): after compinit `_comps[rg]=_ripgrep`; first call -> no `_arguments` invocation and `_comps[rg]` silently rebound to `_rg`; second call -> `_arguments` runs. Baseline tail `_rg "$@"` -> `_arguments` runs on the first call.

Probes: funcstack[1] is `/proc/self/fd/11` for `source <(...)`, `_probe` for `source _probe`, `./_probe` for `source ./_probe`, `(eval)` for eval, `_probe` for autoload; zsh_eval_context[-1] is `file`, `file`, `file`, `eval`, `loadautofunc` (zsh-style) / `evalautofunc` (ksh-style) respectively.

Scratch run with `[[ ${zsh_eval_context[-1]} != file ]] || (( ! ${+functions[compdef]} ))`: relative source rc=0 and registered; zsh-style and ksh-style autoload list args; process-substitution source registers; ci/test-complete emulation prints 341 arg specs, same as the original.

native_payload.intent: Make the generated zsh completion script loadable directly via `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` (issue #2956) by replacing the unconditional trailing `_rg "$@"` with a guard: run the function only when executing as the autoloaded `_rg` function or when `compdef` is absent (the ci/test-complete harness), otherwise register it with `compdef _rg rg`. Must not regress the fpath/autoload install path or ci/test-complete. FAQ.md is updated to recommend the fpath method, explain adding the directory to fpath, and offer the source one-liner as a slower alternative.

residual_risks: A shell with `setopt ksh_arrays` active when the script is sourced prints `<file>:441: bad output format specification` from `(( ! $+functions[compdef] ))` (once the subscript no longer binds, `[compdef]` is parsed as an arithmetic output-base spec); registration still succeeds because the failed test falls through to `compdef _rg rg`. Narrow and cosmetic; bracing the expansions as in finding #4 removes it. (correctness)
KSH_AUTOLOAD installs invoke `_arguments` twice on the first completion (the load-time `_rg "$@"` plus zsh's own call). Identical to the base tail, so not reported as a finding. (adversarial)
All empirical checks ran on zsh 5.8.1 only; funcstack / zsh_eval_context semantics on the zsh 4.x versions the script still special-cases (rg.zsh:353) were not exercised. (correctness, adversarial)

ci/test-complete could not be run end to end (no built rg binary); its `emulate ... no_unset` + `setopt local_options unset` + subshell `source` sequence was reproduced in scratch and yielded 341 spec lines. (correctness, adversarial)

Whether any downstream packaging installs the completion file under a name other than `_rg` was checked only by grep of Cargo.toml, pkg/brew, ci/ and .github/workflows; third-party distro packaging and user-chosen filenames were not surveyed. (adversarial)
testing_gaps: ci/test-complete only exercises the `compdef`-undefined dump branch of the new tail. Nothing automated covers the branches this change is about: that `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` after `compinit` registers `_rg` for `rg` without error, and that the fpath/autoload path still runs the function. A CI step such as `zsh -f -c 'autoload -Uz compinit; compinit -u; source <(rg --generate complete-zsh) && [[ $_comps[rg] == _rg ]]'` would cover the headline scenario once a built `rg` is available.
No test exercises the autoload path with a filename other than `_rg`, sourcing before compinit, or sourcing with a relative path equal to `_rg`.
